title: evidence/widenings-survey.md
body:
# Upstream merge survey: boundary widenings (HEAD → upstream/main 547d7514b)

Read-only. Fixed objects only: HEAD (build/escher-0.4.0), upstream/main 547d7514b, merge base 23b9b26a9.

Counts and the commands that produced them:
- **212** upstream commits: `git log --format='%h %s' HEAD..upstream/main | wc -l`.
- **282** files changed upstream since the merge base: `git diff --stat 23b9b26a9 upstream/main`, where `23b9b26a9` is `git merge-base HEAD upstream/main`. The HEAD→upstream diff (1210 files, +22082/−372379) is mostly the fork's own additions, so it is not the merge's delta.
- **80** of the 212 short SHAs appear somewhere in HEAD's commit messages. I got this by extracting 9-hex tokens from `git log --format=%B HEAD` and matching them against the 212. `git cherry HEAD upstream/main` marks all 212 `+` because the picks were squashed, so patch-ids do not match. Being named in a message does not prove a commit was taken: 286874cc1 (Dioxus 0.8) and ea07ee716 (wpt skia) are named, but HEAD still pins Dioxus 0.7.3 and its wpt runner has no skia feature. For that reason every "HEAD has it?" below was checked with `git diff HEAD upstream/main -- <path>`.

## Widenings

- **CDP server: a new TCP listener, a new crate and a new carrier of page content**
  - Commits: a1670ef1b "Add Chrome DevTools Protocol server (#572)", ad130c16a, 2c929697a, 2ee31e656, 5a486f629, 3f85506dc, 9645839bb.
  - Sites:
    - `packages/blitz-vibey-cdp-server/src/transport.rs:29`: `TcpListener::bind(&addr)`. Each connection is served on its own thread (`:41`). It serves HTTP `/json`, `/json/list` and `/json/version` (`:97-140`), the frontend's files (`:144`), and a WebSocket upgrade (`:165-176`).
    - `src/lib.rs:117`: `start_listening(addr: &str)` is `pub`, so an embedder can pass any address. blitz-shell passes `127.0.0.1:{port}` (`packages/blitz-shell/src/devtools.rs:84`).
  - Access control: none. There is no Origin check and no authentication. Any local process, and any web page able to open `ws://127.0.0.1:PORT`, gets a CDP session.
  - What goes out: `/json/list` returns each document's `title` and `url` (`transport.rs:110-114`). The session sends the DOM (`DOM.getDocument`, `DOM.getOuterHTML`, attributes, text), computed and matched styles, box models and `Page.getResourceTree`'s url (`src/session/{dom,css,page}.rs`). That is page content leaving on a new carrier.
  - What comes in: `DOM.setOuterHTML` (parses caller HTML into the document, `session/dom.rs:196`), `DOM.setAttributeValue`, `DOM.setAttributesAsText`, `DOM.setNodeValue`, `DOM.removeNode`, `DOM.moveTo`, `CSS.setStyleTexts`, `CSS.addRule` and `CSS.setRuleSelector`. All of these mutate the live document.
  - `Runtime.evaluate` and `Runtime.callFunctionOn` are stubs that answer `undefined` (`session/page.rs:25`), so they execute no script.
  - Panic paths: `.unwrap()` on a mutex (`lib.rs:100`) and on connection lookups (`lib.rs:224`, `:242`). The HTTP head is capped at 16 KiB (`transport.rs:70`).
  - Content in logs, on target `blitz_vibey_cdp_server`, not an `escher_*` target:
    - `transport.rs:224` and `:228` warn with the raw WebSocket message `{text}`;
    - `lib.rs:215` traces `command.params`;
    - `lib.rs:404` traces every outgoing message;
    - `transport.rs:178` logs the request `path`.
  - Paragraph touched: §Surfaces — "No served network API, port or auth exists", and "A new socket, port, IPC endpoint or credential path is an arch §Occupied Resources + security-plan amendment first". CLAUDE.md also says "The driver session's Unix socket is the one listener".
  - HEAD has it? **No.** The crate is absent at HEAD, and `Cargo.toml`'s members gain `packages/blitz-vibey-cdp-server` in `git diff HEAD upstream/main -- Cargo.toml`.

- **`BLITZ_CDP_PORT`: a new env read that starts the listener**
  - Commit: a1670ef1b.
  - Sites: `packages/blitz-shell/src/devtools.rs:61`, `std::env::var("BLITZ_CDP_PORT")`, called from `packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:58` on every `BlitzApplication::new` under `#[cfg(feature = "devtools")]`. An unparsable value is echoed to stderr (`devtools.rs:65`, `eprintln!("CDP: invalid BLITZ_CDP_PORT: {port}")`).
  - Paragraph touched: §Secrets — "env reads are `WPT_DIR`, `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML`, `HOME`, … only".
  - HEAD has it? **No** (`packages/blitz-shell/src/devtools.rs` is +208 lines in the HEAD→upstream diff).

- **`BLITZ_DEVTOOLS_FRONTEND_DIR`: a new env read and a new file-read path served over TCP**
  - Commit: d63145027 "Open DevTools from Blitz, with an embedded DevTools frontend (#1452)".
  - Sites:
    - `packages/blitz-vibey-cdp-server/src/frontend.rs:10` (`FRONTEND_DIR_VAR`), `:27` and `:45`;
    - `:46`: `std::fs::read(Path::new(&dir).join(path))`, where `path` is the HTTP request path. It is guarded only by refusing empty and `..` segments (`:39-43`).
  - Effect: any file under the env-named directory is served to any TCP client.
  - Paragraph touched: §Secrets (env list), and §Untrusted input, "do not route agent- or user-supplied URLs through it without a decision recorded".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **`webbrowser`: launches an external browser on a URL**
  - Commits: d63145027 and 5be96ed0e.
  - Sites: `packages/blitz-shell/src/devtools.rs:114` and `:119-120` (`webbrowser::open_browser(Browser::Chrome, &url)`, then `webbrowser::open(&url)`). The URL is `frontend_url(addr, target_id)`, a loopback URL.
  - Prints: `:117` and `:124` `eprintln!` the URL. That is a print site carrying a `url`, outside `tracing`.
  - `webbrowser` itself is already in HEAD's lock (1.2.4); what is new is this call site.
  - Paragraph touched: §Surfaces (a new process-spawning crossing). The CLAUDE.md log rule lists `url`.
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **`devtools` features: which builds include the CDP server by default**
  - Commits: a1670ef1b, d63145027 and 5be96ed0e.
  - `packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml`: `devtools = ["dep:blitz-vibey-cdp-server","dep:webbrowser"]` and `embedded-devtools-frontend`. Neither is in shell's default (`["accessibility","file-dialog"]`).
  - `packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:58-59`: `devtools` and `embedded-devtools-frontend`, not in its default (`:13`).
  - `packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:46`: `devtools = []`.
  - `apps/browser/Cargo.toml:13`: default includes `"devtools", "embedded-devtools-frontend"`. **The `blitz` browser binary therefore ships the listener, the env read and the frontend by default.** It also gains an "Open DevTools" menu item (`apps/browser/src/toolbar.rs:269-316`).
  - `apps/readme/Cargo.toml:43-44` and `examples/todomvc/Cargo.toml:32-35` declare the features but do not make them default.
  - `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` does not mention devtools, and neither do escher-driver or blitz-test-harness.
  - Keyboard shortcuts: with `devtools`, Dioxus Native apps open devtools on F12, Cmd+Option+I or Ctrl+Shift+I by default (`packages/dioxus-native/src/config.rs:45`, `src/shortcut.rs`, `src/dioxus_application.rs:101`).
  - Paragraph touched: §Surfaces, as above.
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **`blitz-chrome-devtools-frontend` 0.1.0: a new registry crate**
  - Commit: d63145027.
  - What it is: a crates.io crate, lock checksum `ada3ec88…`, whose one dependency is `brotli-decompressor`. It embeds about 2 MB that unpack to about 11 MB at runtime (`frontend.rs:57-64`), and that bundle is served to clients.
  - Its source is not in `~/.cargo/registry/src`, so **its contents and any build script are not measurable read-only**.
  - `deny.toml` gains the licence `CDLA-Permissive-2.0` (62715e975; the diff since the merge base shows `+ "CDLA-Permissive-2.0"`).
  - Paragraph touched: §Dependencies — "still review new crates by hand".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **`tungstenite` 0.30.0: a new direct dependency of the CDP server**
  - Commit: a1670ef1b.
  - Site: `Cargo.toml:164` (`tungstenite = "0.30"`), used by `blitz-vibey-cdp-server`. The upstream lock holds both 0.29.0 and 0.30.0; HEAD has 0.28.0, through dioxus-devtools.
  - It is the WebSocket server half of the new listener; it does not widen anything on its own.
  - HEAD has it? **No** (0.30).

- **`floem-editor-core`: a new git (non-registry) dependency**
  - Commits: 60c3baffd "Add parley_code_editor, a standalone code editing control (#1424)" and 1a7ec714e.
  - Sites:
    - `packages/parley_code_editor/Cargo.toml`: `floem-editor-core = { git = "https://github.com/lapce/floem", rev = "1351ffb162faeb8be983f1301d718a0d5fb59c27" }`;
    - upstream `Cargo.lock:3340`: `source = "git+https://github.com/lapce/floem?rev=1351ffb…"`, with no checksum.
  - Reach:
    - it is a workspace member (`Cargo.toml:18`);
    - there is no `default-members`, so `cargo build --workspace`, the `--locked` legs and the lockfile all include it;
    - nothing depends on it (`git grep parley_code_editor upstream/main -- '*.toml'` matches only the members line);
    - `publish = false`.
  - It also brings `syntaxmate =0.3.0`, a new registry crate pinned exactly, with bundled grammars and themes.
  - Its examples (`examples/editor.rs`) read a file path and set the clipboard. They are examples only.
  - Paragraph touched: §Dependencies — "the workspace takes no git dependency … save Taffy alone". CLAUDE.md says the same: "the taffy crate alone excepted".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **Engine change for every document: generated DOM events queued on the document, and focus changes now fire DOM events**
  - Commits: 5d4a1f7b2 "Queue generated DOM events on the document (#1643)", 2c76b3f3c, b4ad543de.
  - Sites in upstream `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`:
    - `:720` `queue_event` (bounded at 1024, `:732`; scroll events coalesced, `:721-729`);
    - `:740` `queue_ua_event`;
    - `:749` `pop_pending_event`.
  - `:1821` `clear_focus` now **queues Blur and FocusOut**. `:1847` `set_focus_to` queues blur, focusout, focus and focusin.
  - `events/driver.rs:391` `flush_pending_events` caps at 1024 per flush. It is called from `dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:278-285` and from `ScriptDocument::poll`.
  - Effect: programmatic focus (`element.focus()`, autofocus, `NodeHandle::set_focus`) now fires events to page scripts and app handlers.
  - Paragraphs this contradicts:
    - §Untrusted input (inert): "the clear firing no DOM `blur` or `focusout`".
    - §Untrusted input (select): "focusing with no click, so no DOM focus events on a single select either". Under upstream, `focus_select` going through `set_focus_to` would fire them.
  - HEAD has it? **No** (`git grep queue_event HEAD -- packages` finds nothing).

- **Engine change for every document: script-dispatched events read `isTrusted = false`**
  - Commit: 5d4a1f7b2.
  - Sites:
    - `packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs`: `EventDispatchSource {Input, UserAgent, Script}` and `is_trusted()`;
    - `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/event.rs:244`;
    - `src/runtime/events.rs`, which now passes `event.is_trusted()`.
  - Effect: a page-script API reading changes. This narrows behaviour, but it changes a recorded fact.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "every runtime event has `isTrusted = true`".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **Engine change for every document: a cancelled pointerup still dispatches a click**
  - Commits: 2f8623555 "Handle a cancelled pointerup in the document (#1640)" and c3ef5c86f "Handle a cancelled pointerdown in the document (#1641)".
  - Sites:
    - `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:106-130`: on `default_prevented`, PointerDown calls `record_pointerdown` and PointerUp calls `handle_pointerup(.., true)`;
    - `events/pointer.rs:577`: `do_click = drag_mode == None && (!default_prevented || event.is_mouse())`, then `queue_ua_event(target, Click)` at `:602`.
  - Effect: a page that `preventDefault()`s a mouse pointerup now still gets a Click, which runs `handle_click`. That means checkbox and radio toggles with their `change`, button submit and link navigation.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "dispatch a Click (the app's handlers, then `handle_click` — so form submission, link navigation…)", and the checkbox and radio `change` paragraph.
  - HEAD has it? **No** (`record_pointerdown` is absent at HEAD).

- **Engine change for every document: SVG presentation attributes mapped to CSS**
  - Commits: ea7cfe0e3 "Map SVG presentation attributes to CSS (#1593)", 414b89b59 and 0bdfe4fa3.
  - Sites: `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/svg_attrs.rs` (`is_presentation_attribute`, about 45 attribute names) and `stylo/presentational_hints.rs:540`.
  - How it parses: values go through Stylo's `PropertyDeclaration::parse_into`, a typed parse where a failure is dropped, with the document's `UrlExtraData`.
  - Possible new fetch trigger: `mask`, `filter` and `clip-path` accept `url(...)`. A `mask="url(x.png)"` attribute could reach the existing mask-image fetch in `layout/damage.rs:577-618` through `stamped_request`, which keeps the `file:` refusal. Whether inline-SVG children reach that damage-pass fetch is **not measurable read-only**.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "the `font` element's `face` and `size`, `valign`, `cellspacing` and `cellpadding` are read as presentational hints by a typed parse … an engine change for every document".
  - HEAD has it? **No** (`svg_presentation_hint` is absent from HEAD's `stylo.rs`).

- **Engine change for every document: `hr`'s `color`, `noshade` and `size` read as hints**
  - Commit: fb381be2c "Map the hr element's color, noshade and size attributes (#1398)".
  - Site: `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs:318-321` and `:478-480`, plus a UA rule in `assets/default.css`.
  - Paragraph touched: the same presentational-hints paragraph.
  - HEAD has it? **No** (`noshade` is absent from HEAD's `stylo.rs`).

- **What reaches the accessibility tree and the snapshot: `visibility: collapse` excluded**
  - Commit: 5b8e7a268 "Exclude visibility: collapse elements from the accessibility tree (#1647)".
  - Site: `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:194` (`!= Visible`, was `== Hidden`).
  - Effect: this narrows what leaves, but it changes the snapshot's node set for every document, because the snapshot reads the tree.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input (accessibility builder), "The readings exit two ways: the platform accessibility adapter … and the snapshot".
  - HEAD has it? **No** (HEAD's hidden check still compares `== Hidden`).
  - Merge note: upstream's `accessibility.rs` differs from HEAD by about 148 lines that the fork added (aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-invalid, select, label binding, focus filter). The resolution must keep the fork's builder.

- **Accessibility tree refreshed after DOM and focus changes**
  - Commit: be60597f6 "Refresh the AccessKit tree after DOM and focus changes (#1456)".
  - Sites:
    - `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1150` `has_changes()` and `:1155` `clear_changes()`; a `has_changes: bool` replaces `changed_nodes`;
    - `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:441-444`.
  - It moves no new content. It **replaces the fork's ratified change tracking** (`changed_nodes` and `take_changed_nodes`, HEAD `document.rs:400` and `:1557`, which the snapshot diff and the `View::poll` refresh rely on). Listed here because it changes when the tree reaches the adapter for every document.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "the headless half — the tree the shell hands the adapter".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **TLS backend switched to rustls with the platform verifier**
  - Commit: 62715e975 "Switch to rustls everywhere except android".
  - Site: `packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml` (`reqwest` features drop `native-tls`; `[target.'cfg(not(target_os="android"))'] reqwest features=["rustls"]`).
  - New lock crates: `aws-lc-rs` 1.18.2, `aws-lc-sys` 0.46.0 (a C library built at compile time), `rustls-platform-verifier` 0.7.1, and through it `rustls-native-certs` and `webpki-root-certs`.
  - Effect: certificate validation for every remote fetch now goes through a different trust path.
  - Paragraph touched: §Dependencies — "still review new crates by hand", plus the new `CDLA-Permissive-2.0` licence in `deny.toml`.
  - HEAD has it? **No** (HEAD's blitz-net still lists `"native-tls"`).

- **Build-time: skia becomes a default in the browser and the WPT runner**
  - Commits: 74861e747 "Browser App: use Skia as the default renderer (#1472)" and ea07ee716 / e7cca1d37 (wpt).
  - Sites: `apps/browser/Cargo.toml:13` (`default = ["skia", …]`) and `wpt/runner/Cargo.toml` (`default = ["cpu","tiny-skia","skia"]`).
  - Effect: `cargo build --workspace` would compile `skia-bindings` 0.157.0, which is already in HEAD's lock but not built by default at HEAD. rust-skia's build script normally downloads prebuilt binaries over the network. That script's behaviour is **not measurable here**, because the registry source is absent.
  - New crate: `anyrender_tiny_skia` 0.1.0.
  - Paragraph touched: §Dependencies (locked and reviewed builds).
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

- **Merge hazard on a ratified loosening guard: the stamped request**
  - Commit: f0d7aeac9 "Refuse @import rules whose URL does not parse (#1677)". This is itself a narrowing that removes a panic on remote CSS.
  - Sites:
    - upstream `packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:31-32` is `stamped_request(url, signal)` → `Request::get(url)`, with no initiator;
    - HEAD `net.rs:31-36` is `stamped_request(url, signal, initiator)` under `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`;
    - upstream has no `packages/blitz-dom/clippy.toml`, while HEAD's bans `Request::get`.
  - Why it matters: upstream's hunk at `net.rs:213-239` touches the `stamped_request` call inside `request_stylesheet`, and its new test builds `StylesheetLoader` without `document_url`. A conflict resolved toward upstream would drop the initiator stamp, and the test will not compile on the fork.
  - Upstream also removes `FileForbidden` and `document_may_load` from `blitz-traits` and `blitz-net` in the HEAD→upstream diff. Those are fork-only, so a three-way merge keeps them unless a hunk conflicts.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "blitz-dom builds a sub-resource request only through the one constructor that stamps its loading document as the initiator".
  - HEAD has it? The @import fix: **No**. The guard: HEAD only.

- **Merge hazard: change synthesis on checkbox and radio input**
  - Commit: 5d4a1f7b2. It touches `blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/events.rs` next to upstream's still-present `target_is_checkbox_or_radio` change synthesis, which the fork deleted.
  - Effect: a resolution that keeps upstream's block makes a page hear two `change` events.
  - Paragraph touched: §Untrusted input — "`blitz-vibey-script`'s runtime synthesizing none".
  - HEAD has it? HEAD has the deletion. Upstream still carries the block (`git diff HEAD upstream/main -- packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/events.rs` shows `+ target_is_checkbox_or_radio`).

- **CI: an unpinned action**
  - Site: upstream `.github/workflows/ci.yml` adds `uses: nttld/setup-ndk@v1`, a tag and not a 40-hex SHA (diff since the merge base).
  - Paragraph touched: §Dependencies — "Every action a CI workflow uses is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA".
  - HEAD has it? **No.**

## Not widenings checked

- **DevtoolsProvider** (73ff15c0d, 3d65a8f1f, 98ab397de). `blitz-traits/src/devtools.rs:37-95` and `blitz-dom/src/config.rs:72-73` (`#[cfg(feature = "devtools")]`). The records carry `NodeId`s and an attribute *name* (`SmolStr`) only: no value, text or URL. The trait is an in-process embedder hook with no carrier, so it only becomes a crossing through the CDP server above. HEAD has it? No.
- **`ScriptDocument::runtime_limits_mut`** (c86d84d0b), `blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:279`. An embedder-only Rust API that exposes Boa's `RuntimeLimits`. Page scripts cannot reach it, and it bounds scripts rather than widening anything. HEAD has it? No.
- **CSSStyleDeclaration accessors** (efdc5472a). A page-script API, but **already at HEAD**: `bootstrap/style.js` is not in the HEAD→upstream diff.
- **Empty `alt` → decorative** (e65ec76e1). This changes a role, not content. **Already at HEAD** (HEAD `accessibility.rs:534-536`).
- **mimalloc** (9eeebb302). **Already at HEAD**: `apps/browser` has `mimalloc` in its default at both, and the lock has 0.1.52 at both. It is an allocator with no I/O.
- **External images in SVG and feImage** (7b8712cba, 1311a45e4). **Already at HEAD** (HEAD `mutator.rs:420,1215,1471`) and already ratified in security.md.
- **CSS masks, SVG filters, text-shadow, mix-blend-mode** (a946a0a7b, 84dec072b, 795cddd5d, bd05d74b2, 6fca6308d). Paint only. The mask-image fetch already exists at HEAD (`mask_images` is in HEAD `damage.rs` and `element.rs`). Filters render through anyrender_svg, and feImage goes through the existing path. None of them reads a new external resource. The one exception is the attribute route noted under the SVG presentation entry.
- **`NetHandler::error` and stylesheet failure** (f6edb9701). Already at HEAD; `blitz-traits/src/net.rs`'s `error` is not in the HEAD→upstream diff. The two loopback `TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")` calls in blitz-net's `#[cfg(test)]` are already registered as test-only.
- **`MULTI_DOC_*` env reads and `paint_bench`'s `std::fs::read`.** Both already at HEAD and registered: `examples/multi_doc.rs` and `paint_bench.rs` are not in the HEAD→upstream diff.
- **Clipboard via winit** (527394724). Clipboard moves from the opt-in `clipboard`/arboard feature to winit's async `request_clipboard_text` and `UiEvent::Paste(String)` (`blitz-traits/src/events.rs:74`). The same paste and copy content was default-on before, so this is a transport change and not a new read. HEAD has it? No.
- **Wheel phase and source on `NativeWheelData`** (13fa9ace8). Gesture enums go to Dioxus app handlers; no page content. HEAD has it? No.
- **`LayoutPassState` and `Node::svg_source` made public** (1e61a279b). Rust API only.
- **`svg_source` namespace declarations** (8228d15f3). Internal serialisation fed to usvg; nothing leaves.
- **iOS UIKit AccessKit adapter** (3ddd337c7, `accesskit_xplat/src/platform_impl/ios.rs`). The same ratified adapter crossing on a platform the fork does not build.
- **Scroll changes** (0958b3d4c, f99630e1e, bb611089c, e1c32e379, e5305a4c1, 0980cce5f). Scroll and overscroll behaviour only; no new content or read path. They do touch `scrolling.rs`, which the fork widened (`scroll_into_view`), so expect conflicts. e5305a4c1 and 0980cce5f are already at HEAD.
- **"Copying from a text input doesn't fire an input event"** (f8f9a26f6). Removes an event (a narrowing).
- **`js_framework_benchmark` example** (242eb0670). A new auto-discovered example of the root crate, with `rand 0.9` as a dev-dependency. No env, network or file read was found in it when I scanned the merge-base diff for `env::var`, `TcpListener` and `fs::read`.
- **Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3** (286874cc1). A dependency move, not a boundary widening, but HEAD pins 0.7.3, so this is a large semantic merge for dioxus-native-dom (stable ids, `keyboard_compat.rs` removed, `mutation_buffer.rs` added).

## Sticky

**No.** The upstream delta does not implement scroll-dependent `position: sticky` (issue #887).
- `git log -S'Sticky' HEAD..upstream/main` and `git log -i -G'sticky' HEAD..upstream/main -- packages` each return only f9d0e8c76, "Paint positioned descendants of static boxes with their positioned ancestor". That commit treats sticky like relative for paint order, with no scroll offset.
- The sticky sites in upstream/main all classify sticky alongside static or relative; none computes an offset against a scroll container:
  - `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/paint_tree.rs:476-481` (`is_in_flow_positioned`: Relative | Sticky), `:506` and `:530`;
  - `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:515` and `:1385` (sticky creates a stacking context);
  - `layout/construct.rs:368`;
  - `resolved_style.rs:654`.
- `packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:309` maps `stylo::Position::Sticky => taffy::Position::Sticky`. That line is identical at HEAD (`convert.rs:308`), and Taffy is pinned to the same rev a3997d55 on both sides.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs` and the scroll commits (0958b3d4c, f99630e1e, bb611089c, e1c32e379) contain no "sticky" at all.

## 2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts — Standard Contracts: 3 row(s)
**Section:** Standard Contracts
**Change:** ~ decision/accessibility-tree-refresh-on-change · rule: was «On a poll that reported work the shell drains the document's changed set, with or without the accessibility feature, and hands the adapter a fresh tree when the set was non-empty.»; now «On a redraw, after resolve, the shell hands the adapter a fresh tree built from the wrapping document when the document's changed set is non-empty, then clears the set; a poll refreshes nothing.»
~ contract/accessibility-tree/platform-refresh · promise: was «blitz-shell refreshes the platform accessibility tree when a poll took a non-empty changed set.»; now «blitz-shell refreshes the platform accessibility tree on a redraw, after resolve, when the changed set is non-empty, and then clears the set.»
~ contract/event-dispatch/focus-change · promise: was «A focus change dispatches blur, focusout, focus, focusin.»; now «A focus change, a programmatic one included, dispatches blur, focusout, focus, focusin; only the focus fix-up under inert and the driver's select focus dispatch none.»
**Why:** decision/accessibility-tree-refresh-on-change: View::poll no longer refreshes the accessibility tree; View::redraw pushes it after resolve when has_changes() and clears the set, so the poll-site rule is false.
contract/accessibility-tree/platform-refresh: The refresh site moved from the poll to the redraw after resolve, so the promise naming the poll is false.
contract/event-dispatch/focus-change: set_focus_to and clear_focus now queue the four focus events while two silent paths remain, which the row states less. — resolved by the operator (Q1): relayed verbatim by the overseer, 2026-11-19, inputs#I4: his answer to W5 (card confirmed by the operator, 2026-11-20)

- Hidden: `hidden` / `display:none` / `visibility:hidden` / `visibility:collapse` exclude the subtree — an `option` of a `select`, its child or under its `optgroup` (`is_select_option`), excepted from `display: none`, which every option of a single-choice select but its chosen one computes and a `multiple` select's rows do not: it stays in the tree, `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still excluding it; `aria-hidden` marks hidden; an element carrying `inert` is excluded with its subtree too, and so from the snapshot, and a hit passes through it, removing `inert` restoring the tree and the hit (the `inert` read ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); a native checkbox or radio keeps its checked state with no box, so a click on its label toggles it even when it is hidden by `display: none` (ratified as upstream's behaviour).

- Platform: accesskit_xplat adapters (windows, macos, unix, android, null); ActionRequested and AccessibilityDeactivated are unhandled TODOs; the tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and pushed again in a redraw, after style resolve, only when the document's changed set, taken and cleared by that redraw, was non-empty, a poll pushing no tree — a focus move, a checked change, a rewritten name, a text control's input, a select's changed choice, a single select's list opening or closing and other mutations mark it, a page scroll or a move that closes a list marking its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, while a highlight or a wheel move inside a list marks nothing and a pointer move alone does not — through `Document::accessibility_tree` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; before 2026-10-07 the poll-time refresh never ran; no windowed witness on the dev host — still owed at the platform adapter, the stand building no adapter, kept so on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next), an active assistive technology this version does not reach; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions both halves are proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes: on Counter, after a drained changed set, each Tab of the whole `tab_order` and an Enter on `counter-increment` leave `has_changes()` true, and the tree read through `&dyn Document` reads the new focus stop and `counter-value`'s new name). A harness settle neither reads nor drains that changed set, and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — a check reading the flag as "this step changed something" drains first. Names come from text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label` and `<label>` association (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label); since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks both (accname 2B) — its loop runs after the `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by` and pushes the referenced nodes, the `aria-label` staying the fallback when the targets hold none — and that text reaches the snapshot `name`. The seven_guis stand names no `accessibility` feature in its own manifest — dioxus-native-dom's reaches it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile the accessibility modules — and builds no platform adapter (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` in neither graph), so the stand binary gives no assistive technology a tree; re-read at 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, when escher-driver took `serde_json` as a fourth dependency (one lock line, no package), no platform adapter joins the stand graph.

Its wire (`v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) carries `hello`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `call`: a call brings an element id and typed text in, and its answer takes ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text and the diff out — a second widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10) — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, the screen's pixels: an accepted `screenshot`'s PNG as base64 inside its JSON line, the whole screen or one element's visible part, a password input in it painted masked, a shot of an open select list also taking a page's option labels and group `label`s out as pixels with the shot's fields unmoved (a boundary widening, ratified), under the unchanged answer bound (the in-band image the founder chose, 2026-10-12), a `lint`'s findings — stable ids, closed defect words and numbers — and, since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers, an accepted `layout`'s readings — ids, closed words and numbers, never a `NodeId`, text or value — and, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph, an accepted `graph`'s line `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}`: ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the closed flag words `undeclared` · `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a control value, typed text or `NodeId` (a boundary widening, ratified), and, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here, an accepted `actions`'s line `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}`: ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, the table's verb words and closed cause words (a cause left out when absent; every listed node carries `layout` with no cause), never a control value, typed text or `NodeId` (a boundary widening, ratified); inside the text and the diff three state readings (selected, pressed, invalid) and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, a changed node's `differs` cross as closed words and booleans, the select list crossing only as a row's own `bounds` in the snapshot, the diff (`differs` naming `bounds`, a closed set) and a `layout` answer, as the `layout` answer's select-list placing word, and as pixels in a shot — `NodeState` holding no field of it, `NODE_FIELDS` fourteen (`clickable`, a closed bool, after `focused`), no `expanded` node key, its highlighted row in no snapshot and no tree — inside the ratified crossing, on his ruling of 2026-10-10, which set the rule: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening, while authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is; no `NodeId` crosses. The MCP surface was the next such crossing, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10): the `escher-session mcp` role (`escher_driver::serve_mcp`) carries the same content — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, the screen as an MCP `image` block (a PNG, base64, a password input in it painted masked, an open list's option labels and group `label`s in it as pixels, a boundary widening ratified; the in-band image the founder chose, 2026-10-12), and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`'s and the session errors' fixed table text, the program's own `'static` text inside the ratified carrier (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12) — to the MCP client that spawned it, over its own stdin and stdout — no listener, port or socket, no authentication beyond holding its stdio — a request line at most 65,536 bytes (longer: read, dropped, `-32700`), the request `id` echoed only as an integer or a string of at most 128 bytes, a result at most 1,048,576 bytes (one that holds an image measured by its whole written form, a text-only one by its text), every protocol error a fixed code and message with no `data`, and a notification running nothing; `serde_json` reads its requests and writes nothing. Since 2026-10-19-session-recording a kept check carries call content at rest (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A · F2 B): under `--record <dir>` (`start`, the host role, the `mcp` role) or `Session::recording_into` or an exploration's record directory, one `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, `create_new`, never replaced) per recorded session, each explored path its own, in a `0700` launcher-named directory (a group- or other-open one refused `record-dir-not-private`, status 3, nothing written or spawned) — an opening record of the app label and the format, then per answered call its verb, arguments (the ids named, `press` keys, `advance` ms, text typed into unmasked controls; a masked or unresolved `type`'s text as `MASKED_STAND_IN`, never the text, its length or a digest of it), acceptance, an FNV-1a 64 digest of its answer and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the answer itself as `answer` — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier (a password's or file input's value as `MASKED_VALUE`), a shot's as `{"width","height"}` with no `png` — so the screens' readings (ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings, a `graph` answer's UI graph, a `layout` step's whole answer (ids, closed words and numbers; its replay stopping on a changed placed value) and an `actions` answer (ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, the table's verb words and closed cause words), never a control value or typed text — a boundary widening, ratified) at rest, never a pixel (each answer kept whole, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F3 B); never logged, no tool call, verb, argument or field names the directory; the one exception to a kept check's owner-only medium is the two committed stand-Counter checks `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` (git mode `100644`, written by `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/record_checks.sh`; no typed text, host path, name or secret and no `screenshot` step), a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-19, F1 A) — a check of any other session stays owner-only and is never committed; a failed write or a passed bound (400 records, 1,048,576 bytes) ends the recording, its check removed; a kept check's bytes are untrusted, read by the strict `Check::from_bytes` (closed keys, the opening `start` record's `format` 1 or absent read as 1, any other value of whatever JSON type refused `malformed` holding nothing of the bytes, `tool` one of the eleven instance verbs, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `answer` required and a JSON object, else `malformed` holding nothing of the file, no panic path), each step still validated inside `Session::run`; since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the `escher-session coverage <app> <check>...` role (no `--session` or `--record`, no socket) is a second reader of caller-named checks, each read through `File::open(..).take(MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1)` then `Check::from_bytes`, a file that cannot be read, one past the bound, one that is no check or a check of another app refused `malformed` (status 1) holding nothing of the path or the file, each accepted check replayed on a fresh in-process session, its one stdout line `{"unexercised":[{"id","owner","event"}],"checks":n,"held":m}` holding ids, owner ids, event names and the two counts only (no control value, typed text, path or `NodeId`), the role adding no span — a boundary widening, ratified; an exploration's report holds only closed endings, indices, calls and booleans, never a panic payload, `NodeId`, screen text or screen digest, and is never logged or printed; `Check::replay` runs each kept step's call through `Session::run` alone, nothing on a session of another app, and stops at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, its `Replay` and `Change` holding bools, counts and closed schema words only. The next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question. A request line over 16,384 bytes or outside the grammar is refused and runs nothing; an answer is bounded at 1,048,576 bytes (`oversize` past it — the call ran and is not rolled back), and a call after which the host's recording ended is answered the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` in place of its answer, the call having run. A host that has answered no request for its idle expiry (1,800 s) ends as on `stop`; every answered request — an `attach` or a `status` included — starts the count again.

- The dependency audit is cargo-deny (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit`, config `deny.toml`; the local `fast` leg runs no audit, so run it before a push — CI can go red on advisories published after the base's green audit with `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` unchanged): an advisory it fires on is fixed by a semver-compatible update, or ignored by ID with a written reason that names its owner as a residual row by its id (no product file names the residuals file) — never a blanket allow, never `unmaintained`/`unsound` set to none. Since 2026-10-14-quality-gates it checks advisories and licences over the whole workspace's graph (`--workspace --all-features`): paste (RUSTSEC-2024-0436) reaches it and is ignored by ID, its drop owned by a `residual` row in the store; ttf-parser 0.25.1's RUSTSEC-2026-0192 (unmaintained, no patched release, reached only through winit 0.31.0-beta.4 → winit-wayland → sctk-adwaita → ab_glyph → owned_ttf_parser, no fix reachable without a lone bump of the coupled winit pin) is ignored by ID, a bounded deferral; zip 2.4.2's RUSTSEC-2026-0367 · RUSTSEC-2026-0368 · RUSTSEC-2026-0369 (the three on the founder's «Игнор по ID (Рекомендую)», 2026-10-17) and RUSTSEC-2026-0429 (`ZipArchive::extract` aborting the process on a symlink entry with a large declared size; external decay) — each fixed only in zip 9.0, reached only through `anyrender_serialize 0.8.0` ← `browser`, which reads entries `by_name` and never calls `extract`, no fixed release reachable — are ignored by ID, their drop owned by the store's `residual` row `res-h7acz56c`; zvariant 5.15.0's RUSTSEC-2026-0370, zbus_names 4.3.4's RUSTSEC-2026-0371 and zvariant_derive 5.15.0's RUSTSEC-2026-0372 (unmaintained, folded into zbus 6.0.0, reached only through zbus 5.19 + atspi 0.29 under accesskit_unix 0.24.0 ← accesskit_xplat ← blitz-shell, no fix reachable) are ignored by ID on the operator's word under the playbook's External decay pattern (2026-10-17), dropped when accesskit_unix moves to zbus 6, owned by a `residual` row in the store; libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1's RUSTSEC-2026-0459, reached only through `rusqlite` 0.32 ← `browser-persistence` ← `browser`, is ignored by ID with its written reason since 2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration, owned by a `residual` row in the store until the browser moves to `rusqlite` ≥ 0.41; memmap2 (unsound) is kept out by the `unsound` default, a measured limit owned by a `residual` row in the store — still review new crates by hand.

- `Cargo.lock` is committed; the workspace takes no git dependency, the root manifest included, save Taffy alone, which takes a git source — upstream DioxusLabs/taffy pinned at a full commit rev (a3997d55), no patch section, integrity resting on the rev as its lock entry has no checksum, still passing the lock, audit and MSRV legs; every other crate a crates.io registry version with its checksum in the lockfile; builds pass `--locked` — keep both. Skia is built by default in the browser app and the WPT runner, its build script fetching prebuilt binaries from GitHub releases at build time with no content check — a supply-chain widening by upstream merge, ratified. Every action a CI workflow uses is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA, its ref kept as a trailing comment (`WorkflowPinTest`) — keep it so.

- No mocking library, property-test or snapshot crate is used (blitz-tests carries the assertion crate test-that 0.6.0 with test-that-macro 0.6.0 as dev-dependencies, 0.5.2 until 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts, whose `verify_that!` and `TestResult<()>` upstream's merged checks that use them assert through under the same `#[test]` harness) — stand-ins are hand-written fakes (`RecordingNetProvider` and `ManualNetProvider`, upstream's; escher's one held network stand-in `fixtures::HeldNet`; since 2026-10-20-load-wait `stand_load_wait`'s in-file self-answering `LateNet`, whose `fetch` answers each request from its own thread after a 200 ms sleep; the stand's own `LoadNet`, private to `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, which `stand::boot_load` puts in its options' `net_provider` and which answers the fixed `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms), `is_noop` not overridden; the error-text check's failing page's `FailingNet`, which fails its fetch; a blitz-tests check's hand-written stand-in that reads `file:` loads through blitz-net's real provider, blocking on a current-thread tokio runtime it owns, with blitz-net and tokio taken as blitz-tests dev-dependencies for it (`a_remote_page_reads_no_local_file_and_a_file_page_reads_them_all`); `RecordingShell`, `select_popup`'s own `CountingShell`, blitz-shell's test-local `CountedWakes`, `NoopEventHandler`, probe widgets). A check decodes or encodes a PNG through blitz-tests' `png` dev-dependency, or, in seven_guis, which has none, by a hand base64 reader and the PNG header.
